title_en: Environmental Impact Assessment Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of implementing the sustainable development strategy, preventing adverse environmental impacts resulting from the implementation of plans and construction projects, and promoting the coordinated development of economy, society and the environment.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "environmental impact assessment" means the methods and systems for analyzing, predicting and assessing the environmental impacts that may be caused after the implementation of plans and construction projects, proposing countermeasures and measures for preventing or mitigating adverse environmental impacts, and conducting follow-up monitoring.

Article 3 For plans formulated within the scope specified in Article 9 of this Law, and for projects that have impacts on the environment and are constructed within the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China, an environmental impact assessment shall be conducted in accordance with this Law.

Article 4 An environmental impact assessment must be objective, open and impartial, shall comprehensively consider the possible impacts of the implementation of a plan or construction project on various environmental factors and the ecosystems composed thereof, and shall provide a scientific basis for decision-making.
Article 5 The State encourages relevant entities, experts and the public to participate in environmental impact assessment in appropriate ways.

Article 6 The State shall strengthen the development of a basic database and an evaluation indicator system for environmental impact assessment, encourage and support scientific research on the methods and technical specifications for environmental impact assessment, establish a necessary information sharing system for environmental impact assessment, and enhance the scientific nature of environmental impact assessment.
The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, organize the establishment and improvement of the basic database and the evaluation indicator system for environmental impact assessment.

Article 7 The relevant departments of the State Council, the local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts and their relevant departments shall, during the process of formulating relevant plans for land use and plans for the construction, development and utilization of regions, river basins and sea areas, organize an environmental impact assessment and prepare a chapter or description on the environmental impact of such plan.
A chapter or description on the environmental impact of a plan shall analyze, predict and assess the possible environmental impacts after the implementation of the plan, propose countermeasures and measures for preventing or mitigating adverse environmental impacts, and shall be submitted as a component of the draft plan to the plan approval authority.
The plan approval authority shall not approve a draft plan that does not contain a chapter or description on the environmental impact.

Article 8 The relevant departments of the State Council, the local people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts and their relevant departments shall, for the special plans formulated by them concerning industry, agriculture, animal husbandry, forestry, energy, water conservancy, transportation, urban construction, tourism and natural resources development (hereinafter referred to as special plans), organize an environmental impact assessment before submitting the draft special plan for approval, and submit an environmental impact report to the authority approving the special plan.
A guiding plan among the special plans listed in the preceding paragraph shall undergo an environmental impact assessment in accordance with the provisions of Article 7 of this Law.

Article 9 The specific scope of plans for which an environmental impact assessment is to be conducted in accordance with Articles 7 and 8 of this Law shall be specified by the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, and shall be submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 10 An environmental impact report on a special plan shall include the following:
(1) analysis, prediction and assessment of the possible environmental impacts of implementing the plan;
(2) countermeasures and measures for preventing or mitigating adverse environmental impacts; and
(3) conclusions of the environmental impact assessment.

Article 11 The authority formulating a special plan that may cause adverse environmental impacts and directly involves the environmental rights and interests of the public shall, before submitting the draft plan for approval, hold demonstration meetings, public hearings or adopt other forms to solicit opinions from relevant entities, experts and the public on the draft environmental impact report, except where confidentiality is required under national regulations.
The formulating authority shall seriously consider the opinions of relevant entities, experts and the public on the draft environmental impact report, and shall attach an explanation of whether such opinions have been adopted in the environmental impact report submitted for review.

Article 12 When submitting a draft special plan for approval, the formulating authority shall submit the environmental impact report together with it to the approval authority for review; if the environmental impact report is not submitted, the approval authority shall not grant approval.

Article 13 Before a people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts approves a draft special plan and makes a decision, the competent department of ecology and environment or another department designated by the people's government shall convene representatives of relevant departments and experts to form a review panel to review the environmental impact report. The review panel shall issue a written review opinion.
The experts serving on the review panel specified in the preceding paragraph shall be determined by random selection from the list of experts in relevant specialties within the expert database established in accordance with the provisions of the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council.
The review measures for the environmental impact reports on special plans to be approved by the relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall be formulated by the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 14 If the review panel proposes revision opinions, the authority formulating a special plan shall modify and improve the draft plan in accordance with the conclusions of the environmental impact report and the review opinions, and explain the adoption of the conclusions of the environmental impact report and the review opinions; if not adopted, reasons shall be given.
When approving a draft special plan, the people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts or the relevant department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall take the conclusions of the environmental impact report and the review opinions as an important basis for decision-making.
If the conclusions of the environmental impact report and the review opinions are not adopted during the approval process, an explanation shall be given, and the relevant materials shall be kept on file for future reference.

Article 15 After a plan that has a significant impact on the environment is implemented, the authority that formulated it shall promptly organize a follow-up evaluation of the environmental impact and report the evaluation results to the approval authority; if it is found that there are obviously adverse environmental impacts, it shall promptly propose improvement measures.

Article 16 The State shall exercise classified management over the environmental impact assessment of construction projects based on the degree of their impact on the environment.
The construction entity shall organize the preparation of an environmental impact report, an environmental impact statement, or the filling of an environmental impact registration form (hereinafter collectively referred to as the environmental impact assessment document) in accordance with the following provisions:
(1) for projects that may cause significant environmental impacts, an environmental impact report shall be prepared, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the environmental impacts generated;
(2) for projects that may cause minor environmental impacts, an environmental impact statement shall be prepared, providing an analysis or special evaluation of the environmental impacts generated; and
(3) for projects with very minor environmental impacts that do not require an environmental impact assessment, an environmental impact registration form shall be filled.
The classified management list for environmental impact assessment of construction projects shall be formulated and published by the competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council.

Article 18 The environmental impact assessment of a construction project shall avoid duplication with the environmental impact assessment of a plan.
A plan that is considered a single construction project shall undergo an environmental impact assessment as a construction project and not as a plan.
If a plan that has already undergone an environmental impact assessment contains specific construction projects, the conclusions of the plan's environmental impact assessment shall serve as an important basis for the environmental impact assessment of the construction projects, and the content of the construction project's environmental impact assessment shall be simplified in accordance with the review opinions on the plan's environmental impact assessment.

Article 19 A construction entity may commission a technical entity to conduct an environmental impact assessment for its construction project and prepare an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement; if the construction entity has the technical capability to conduct an environmental impact assessment, it may conduct the assessment by itself and prepare the environmental impact report or environmental impact statement.
The preparation of an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for a construction project shall comply with the relevant national standards, technical specifications and other provisions on environmental impact assessment.
The competent department of ecology and environment of the State Council shall formulate guidelines for capacity building and regulatory measures for the preparation of environmental impact reports and environmental impact statements for construction projects.
A technical entity commissioned by a construction entity to prepare an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for a construction project shall not have any interest relationship with the competent department of ecology and environment or any other relevant approval authority responsible for approving the environmental impact report or environmental impact statement.

Article 20 A construction entity shall be responsible for the content and conclusions of the environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for its construction project; the technical entity commissioned to prepare an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for a construction project shall bear corresponding liability for the report or statement it prepares.
The competent departments of ecology and environment of the people's governments at or above the level of a city divided into districts shall strengthen the supervision, management and quality assessment of entities that prepare environmental impact reports or environmental impact statements for construction projects.
The competent department of ecology and environment responsible for approving an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for a construction project shall record the relevant illegal information of the preparing entity, the person in charge of preparation and the main preparers into their social credit files, include it in the national credit information sharing platform and the national enterprise credit information publicity system, and make it public.
No entity or individual may designate a technical entity to prepare an environmental impact report or environmental impact statement for a construction project for the construction entity.

Article 21 Unless the matter is required to be kept confidential by the State, for a construction project which may cause a major impact on the environment and for which an environmental impact report shall be prepared, the construction entity shall, before submitting the environmental impact report for approval, hold hearings, expert consultation meetings, or adopt other forms to solicit opinions from relevant authorities, experts, and the public.
The environmental impact report submitted by the construction entity for approval shall include an explanation of whether the opinions of relevant authorities, experts, and the public have been adopted or not.

Article 22 The environmental impact report or statement of a construction project shall be submitted by the construction entity to the competent department of ecology and environment with the approving authority for examination and approval in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
The examination and approval of the marine environmental impact report for a marine engineering construction project shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Marine Environmental Protection.
The approving department shall, within sixty days from the date of receipt of the environmental impact report, and within thirty days from the date of receipt of the environmental impact statement, make a decision on approval and notify the construction entity in writing.
The State implements record-filing management for environmental impact registration forms.
No fee shall be charged for the review, examination, and approval of environmental impact reports or statements, or for the record-filing of environmental impact registration forms.

Article 23 The competent department of ecology and environment under the State Council shall be responsible for examining and approving the environmental impact assessment documents for the following construction projects:
(1) construction projects of a special nature, such as nuclear facilities and top-secret projects;
(2) construction projects that cross the administrative boundaries of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government; and
(3) construction projects that require approval by the State Council or by the departments authorized by the State Council.
The approving authority for environmental impact assessment documents of construction projects other than those specified in the preceding paragraph shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government.
Where a construction project may cause adverse environmental impacts across administrative boundaries, and the relevant competent departments of ecology and environment have disputes over the environmental impact assessment conclusions of the project, the environmental impact assessment documents shall be examined and approved by the competent department of ecology and environment at the next higher level common to all parties involved.

Article 24 After the environmental impact assessment document of a construction project has been approved, if the nature, scale, location, production technology adopted, or measures for preventing pollution and ecological damage of the project undergo major changes, the construction entity shall re-submit the environmental impact assessment document for approval.
If a construction project decides to commence construction more than five years after the date of approval of its environmental impact assessment document, the environmental impact assessment document shall be re-examined by the original approving department; the original approving department shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of the environmental impact assessment document of the construction project, notify the construction entity in writing of its review opinion.

Article 25 Where the environmental impact assessment document of a construction project has not been reviewed by the approving department according to law or has been reviewed but not approved, the construction entity shall not commence construction.

Article 26 During the construction of a construction project, the construction entity shall simultaneously implement the environmental protection measures proposed in the environmental impact report, the environmental impact statement, and the approval opinions of the department examining and approving the environmental impact assessment document.

Article 27 Where during the construction or operation of a project, circumstances arise that are inconsistent with the approved environmental impact assessment document, the construction entity shall organize a post-environmental impact assessment, take improvement measures, and report to the original approving department of the environmental impact assessment document and the department examining and approving the construction project for record; the original approving department of the environmental impact assessment document may also require the construction entity to conduct a post-environmental impact assessment and take improvement measures.

Article 28 The competent department of ecology and environment shall track and inspect the environmental impacts after a construction project is put into production or use, and where serious environmental pollution or ecological damage is caused, it shall ascertain the cause and identify the responsibility. Where the environmental impact report or statement of a construction project has serious quality problems such as obviously false basic data, major defects, omissions, or falsifications in content, or incorrect or unreasonable environmental impact assessment conclusions, the legal liability of the construction entity and its relevant responsible persons, as well as the technical entity commissioned to prepare the environmental impact report or statement and its relevant personnel, shall be pursued in accordance with Article 32 of this Law. Where the staff of the approving department neglects their duty or engages in malfeasance by approving an environmental impact report or statement of a construction project that should not have been approved according to law, their legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with Article 34 of this Law.

Article 29 Where a planning compilation authority, in violation of the provisions of this Law, fails to organize an environmental impact assessment, or practices fraud or neglects its duties when organizing an environmental impact assessment, resulting in the environmental impact assessment being seriously inaccurate, the competent persons directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be given administrative sanctions according to law by the higher-level authority or the supervisory authority.

Article 30 Where a planning approval authority illegally approves a draft plan which should have contained a chapter or explanation on environmental impact but does not, or a draft special plan which should have been accompanied by an environmental impact report but is not, the competent persons directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be given administrative sanctions according to law by the higher-level authority or the supervisory authority.

Article 31 Where a construction entity, without submitting the environmental impact report or statement for approval according to law, or without re-submitting or re-applying for review of the environmental impact report or statement in accordance with Article 24 of this Law, commences construction without authorization, the competent department of ecology and environment at or above the county level shall order the cessation of construction, impose a fine of not less than one percent but not more than five percent of the total investment amount of the construction project based on the illegal circumstances and harmful consequences, and may order restoration to the original condition; the competent persons directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel of the construction entity shall be given administrative sanctions according to law.
Where the environmental impact report or statement of a construction project has not been approved or has not been re-examined and approved by the original approving department, and the construction entity commences construction without authorization, the punishment and sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
Where a construction entity fails to file an environmental impact registration form for a construction project according to law, the competent department of ecology and environment at or above the county level shall order the filing to be made and impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan.
Where a construction entity of a marine engineering construction project commits any of the illegal acts listed in this Article, the punishment shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Marine Environmental Protection.

Article 32 Where an environmental impact report or statement of a construction project has serious quality problems such as obviously false basic data, major defects, omissions, or falsifications in content, or incorrect or unreasonable environmental impact assessment conclusions, the competent department of ecology and environment of the people's government at or above the city with districts level shall impose a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan on the construction entity, and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan on the legal representative, principal responsible person, competent persons directly in charge, and other directly responsible personnel of the construction entity.
Where a technical entity commissioned to prepare an environmental impact report or statement violates the relevant State standards and technical specifications for environmental impact assessment, resulting in the environmental impact report or statement it prepares having serious quality problems such as obviously false basic data, major defects, omissions, or falsifications in content, or incorrect or unreasonable environmental impact assessment conclusions, the competent department of ecology and environment of the people's government at or above the city with districts level shall impose a fine of not less than three times but not more than five times the fees collected by the technical entity; if the circumstances are serious, the technical entity shall be prohibited from engaging in the preparation of environmental impact reports or statements; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated.
Where a compiling entity commits the illegal acts specified in the first or second paragraph of this Article, the presiding compiler and the principal compilers shall be prohibited from engaging in the preparation of environmental impact reports or statements for five years; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law, and they shall be permanently prohibited from engaging in the preparation of environmental impact reports or statements.

Article 33 Where a department responsible for reviewing, examining and approving, or filing environmental impact assessment documents of construction projects charges fees in the process of examination, approval, or filing, the higher-level authority or the supervisory authority shall order the refund of such fees; if the circumstances are serious, the competent persons directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be given administrative sanctions according to law.

Article 34 Where staff members of the competent department of ecology and environment or other departments engage in favoritism, abuse their power, dereliction of duty, or illegally approve environmental impact assessment documents of construction projects, they shall be given administrative sanctions according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 35 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on their local actual conditions, require environmental impact assessments to be conducted on plans compiled by the people's governments at the county level within their respective jurisdictions. The specific measures shall be formulated by the provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government with reference to the provisions of Chapter II of this Law.

Article 36 The measures for environmental impact assessment of military facility construction projects shall be formulated by the Central Military Commission in accordance with the principles of this Law.
Article 37 This Law shall come into force as of September 1, 2003.
